title: Bound graph-load validation complexity under high-cardinality snapshots
outcome: Bound graph-load validation complexity under high-cardinality snapshots
acceptance: Hierarchy, lifecycle-proof and relation validation build shared indexes for items, records and blockers once, preserve the current validation and refusal semantics, and run in linear work in the input plus traversed or materialised output (I+R+B+E+P), with aggregate counted element work at most 20*(I+R+B+E+P)+64 rather than per-item scans of those collections.

The scale gate validates the largest snapshot in a predeclared minimal-valid independent-open-root family whose serialized container is at most 134217728 bytes, proves that adding its next member exceeds that limit, and records the family construction, Nmax, bytes and runtime-derived fingerprint before timing; this is the maximum of that declared family, not a global encoding maximum.

The scale gate covers quarter, half and full Nmax plus mixed forest, terminal fanout and concentrated history/relation fixtures; it reports P/(I+R+B+E) and preserves boundary refusals without destination changes. Each declared maximum-fixture validation sample finishes within the predeclared 120-second host budget, excluding fixture construction and destination setup.
